response.answer:
The First-Sentence Perpetual Motion Machine (fictional)

FIGURE 1
```text
[A: illuminated cursor — highlights the opening sentence]
                   ↓
[B: ink-viscosity regulator — thickens the prose]
                   ↓
[C: temporal-dilation dial — slows perceived time]
BACK TO A: the cursor returns to the first sentence, now deemed imperfect
```

CLAIM 1 — An apparatus for converting the intention to write into the perpetual refinement of a single sentence, thereby ensuring the non-completion of any substantial work.

BENCH TEST — In an imagined study, the operator stares at the illuminated cursor. The ink-viscosity regulator, sensing hesitation, subtly thickens the current sentence, making it feel dense and resistant to further progress. The temporal-dilation dial then stretches the perceived minutes into hours, during which the operator revises the same phrase, convinced that a better opening is just one more tweak away. The cursor, finding the sentence still lacking, returns to its starting position.

PULL A PART
A highlights the opening sentence; B thickens the prose; C slows perceived time. Choose which function to interrupt.

Question outside the patent: what is the perceived cost of a perfect first word?

Pull A, B or C and paste this sketch. The bureau will invent an amendment using what remains.
